subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis
description: A 60-second lesson on The Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis.

hook.text: Do Inuit people really see more types of snow because they have more words for it? The debate has raged for a century.

buildup.text: The strong version—language determines thought—is mostly rejected. You can think things you have no word for.

discovery.text: But the weak version holds up: language influences habitual thought. It nudges attention and memory patterns.

twist.text: The Pirahã language has no number words. Speakers struggle with exact quantity tasks that others find trivial.

climax.text: Language doesn't build walls around thought—but it does build highways. It makes some thoughts easier to travel.

punchline.text: Language doesn't trap thought—it tilts it.

quiz.question: What is the current view on the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis?
options: Language influences but doesn't determine thought
Language has no effect on thought
